title: Congress buy-clusters precede 90-day outperformance
hypothesis: A cluster of congressional purchases in a stock over the trailing 90 days predicts that stock beating its sector-median return over the next 90 days.
falsifier: If the top-decile congress-buy basket fails to beat the sector-median forward 90-day return by at least 2 percentage points out-of-sample — after the deflation correction for the declared trial count — the hypothesis is refuted.

lookahead.note: STOCK Act filings lagged to their disclosure date (~45d), not the trade date. A-vs-B truncation test in lookahead-gate/ passed: no future filing date leaks into any forward 90-day window.

evidence: Out-of-sample the top-decile congress-buy basket returned +0.4% vs the sector median over 90 days across all 12 declared trials. The raw in-sample signal (+3.1%) did not survive the deflation correction or the out-of-sample split.
verdict: Refuted. The edge is gone by the time a purchase is public — the ~45-day STOCK Act filing lag means the move is already priced. Written up in full precisely because it was killed: a refuted hypothesis with a clean falsifier is worth more than a supported one with a fuzzy bar.

title: 424B2 structured-note issuance — descriptive map + dealer-hedging test
hypothesis: Aggregate 424B2 structured-note issuance on an underlying creates measurable dealer hedging exposure — issuers hedge the book's embedded short-put/short-call profile in the underlying and its options, leaving a footprint concentrated near barrier/autocall levels and around observation dates. Prediction: underlyings with elevated recent issuance show different realized-vol and price behavior near clustered barrier levels than matched low-issuance controls.
falsifier: No difference between high-issuance and matched low-issuance underlyings' realized-vol/price behavior near clustered barrier levels — after controlling for size, liquidity and options open interest, and after the Bonferroni-style correction for the declared 18 trials (|t| ≥ 2.7) — refutes it.

lookahead.note: 424B2 filings carry a pricing_date (in the document) and an EDGAR acceptance timestamp (file_date), and they differ. The knowledge date used everywhere is the acceptance timestamp, never pricing_date. Research/structured_note_issuance/test_causal_test.py adapts the lookahead-gate/ A-vs-B truncation test to this filing-event signal and passed — 0 mismatches for the shipped acceptance-date-keyed feature; a deliberately leaky pricing_date-keyed sibling was caught, proving the gate has teeth.

evidence: Part A (issuance-by-underlying, barrier/autocall clustering vs spot, issuer markup league table) shipped separately as issue #130 — tools/edgar_scrubber/research_maps.py, gated against synthetic multi-issuer/basket-note data in tools/edgar_scrubber/test_research_maps.py — regardless of Part B per the project's acceptance criteria. Part B's full pipeline (feature computation, matched-control selection, 18 declared trials, verdict logic, look-ahead gate) is implemented and gated in test_causal_test.py against a synthetic universe to prove the mechanism, but has not been run against real filings: no live EDGAR crawl has populated the local scrubber store in this checkout, and no real price/realized-vol/options-OI/ADV universe has been wired in yet.
verdict: Inconclusive — no data yet. Zero real trials have been scored because the local OutputStore is empty and no real underlying universe has been supplied. This is the honest current state, not a placeholder: Research/structured_note_issuance/README.md documents exactly what running `crawl.py` against the saved query plus a real UnderlyingUniverse per symbol would take to turn this into a real supported/refuted/inconclusive verdict — no code changes required to get there. Part A ships today regardless.
